items.text: Strand A: what has been measured about prospective audit and feedback programmes in hospitals (antimicrobial use, clinical outcomes, costs, acceptance and staffing), with particular attention to surgery, intensive care and hospitals under 200 beds?
items.population: Hospitalised patients and the stewardship services that review their antimicrobials
items.concept: Measured outcomes of prospective audit and feedback: use, clinical outcomes, costs, acceptance, staffing
items.context: Hospitals of any size, 2005 onward, English or French
items.outcome: Days of therapy or other use measures as reported

items.text: Strand B: how do prescribers, pharmacists and nurses experience and act on stewardship audit and feedback recommendations, and why do they accept or decline them?
items.population: Prescribers, pharmacists and nurses in hospitals with audit and feedback
items.intervention: Receiving, giving or carrying stewardship recommendations (phenomenon of interest)
items.outcome: Reported reasons for acceptance or refusal, and perceived role of hierarchy, timing and delivery mode
items.context: Studies with interview, focus group, observation or open-text designs; any hospital setting; 2005 onward

finer: Feasible with the library, four pharmacist hours a week, the resident from January and the fellow; interesting to the committee; novel as a two-strand map for this decision; ethical with no participants; relevant to the April meeting.
summary: One PCC question for the measured-outcomes strand and one SPIDER question for the experience strand, kept separate.
